newsitem.title: UK: Sedgwick Transamerica wind up RTI.
newsitem.headline: Sedgwick Transamerica wind up RTI.

text.p: British-based insurance broker Sedgwick said on Monday that its associate River Thames Insurance Co (RTI) would cease underwriting with immediate effect. The company is 49 percent owned by Sedgwick and 51 percent by U.S. financial giant Transamerica Corp.

"Sedgwick expects to receive cash at least equivalent to (RTI's) book value of approximately 28 million stg progressively over a period of time through efficient management of the run-off. The impact on the group's profit and loss account and balance sheet in 1996 is likely to be minimal," the company said in a statement.
The decision had its roots in a move made in 1992 when RTI decided to curtail the level of business underwritten and focus on specialist business, Sedgwick added.
It noted that it had already withdrawn from underwriting in the United States and Bermuda "and this is an appropriate time for the company to withdraw from underwriting in the UK."
River Thames, which operates in the London insurance market underwriting mainly non-marine and marine reinsurance, stopped taking on new business several days ago, industry sources said.
It emloys 46 staff. The underwriters have been offered positions with Australian insurer HIH 's UK division, which will also have the rights to renewals business.

An announcement detailing how the River Thames is to be run-off is expected in the near future. River Thames made profits of 5.1 million stg last year. Net claims outstanding at the end of last year were 150.6 million stg.
Sedgwick's withdrawal from underwriting is now complete.
It sold its Bermudian underwriting business three years ago and put its New Orleans-based "Americas" unit into run-off two years ago.
